experiment_design.technical_details: This experiment tests the hypothesis that gravity is purely geometric (General Relativity) by analyzing high-precision astrometric and spectroscopic data of S-stars orbiting SgrA*. The core technical challenge is fitting orbital parameters while simultaneously solving for post-Newtonian (PN) corrections, specifically the gravitational redshift ($z_{GR}$) and Schwarzschild precession ($\Delta \omega$). We will employ a Bayesian inference framework using Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods to estimate the posterior distributions of PN parameters. The model will include standard Keplerian elements plus relativistic perturbations derived from the Schwarzschild metric. Systematic errors from instrumental calibration (GRAVITY UT baselines) and astrophysical noise (extended mass distribution) will be marginalized over using hierarchical modeling.

experiment_design.methods:
1. Data Preprocessing: Calibrate raw K-band visibility amplitudes and fluxes using transfer function data to correct for atmospheric and instrumental systematics. Extract precise astrometric positions and radial velocities with associated covariance matrices.
2. Orbital Modeling: Implement a relativistic orbital integrator that includes 1st-order Post-Newtonian corrections (Schwarzschild precession and gravitational redshift) as free scaling parameters ($f_{SP}$ and $f_{GR}$). In pure GR, these should equal 1.
3. Bayesian Inference: Use an affine-invariant MCMC sampler (e.g., emcee) to explore the parameter space. Priors will be set based on Newtonian limits and previous observational constraints.
4. Model Comparison: Compute Bayes Factors to compare the pure GR model ($f_{SP}=1, f_{GR}=1$) against alternative models (e.g., modified gravity where $f \neq 1$, or Newtonian only).

baselines: Pure Newtonian Gravity Model: Assumes no relativistic corrections; serves as the null hypothesis for strong-field deviations.
Standard General Relativity (Fixed): Fixes PN parameters to exactly 1; used to calculate goodness-of-fit ($\chi^2$) and residuals.
Extended Mass Distribution Model: Includes a distributed mass component (e.g., stellar cluster, dark matter spike) to test if apparent relativistic effects are mimicked by local mass density.
metrics: Posterior Mean and Credible Intervals for f_SP and f_GR: Quantifies deviation from GR predictions.
Bayes Factor (K): Evaluates statistical preference for GR vs. alternative models.
Reduced Chi-Squared ($\chi^2_\nu$): Assesses the goodness-of-fit for the best-fit model.
Residual Autocorrelation: Checks for unmodeled systematic errors in time-series residuals.
experiments.ablation:
1. Exclude Gravitational Redshift: Fit only astrometric precession to isolate spatial curvature effects.
2. Exclude Extended Mass: Fix extended mass to zero to test sensitivity of PN parameters to background potential assumptions.
3. Subset Analysis: Perform fits using only pre-2018 data vs. full dataset including pericenter passage to evaluate information gain from strong-field regime.
experiments.validation_protocol:
1. Injection-Recovery Tests: Inject synthetic signals with known PN parameters into real noise data to verify parameter recovery accuracy.
2. Cross-Validation: Split data by epoch (pre-pericenter vs. post-pericenter) to ensure consistency of derived parameters.
3. Systematic Error Budget: Propagate calibration uncertainties from K-band visibility data into final parameter posteriors.
